linked_evidence.source_text: Mitochondrial thermogenesis, induced by exothermic ORR (1/2 O2 + 2H+ + 2e- → H2O), relies on the abundant availability of reactants (H+, O2, and electrons) within the mitochondria. Consequently, protonophore-induced mitochondrial thermogenesis is contingent upon a well-maintained oxygen supply and efficient electron transport in the mitochondria.

Overall, here we confirmed that every component (i.e., proton, oxygen, and electrons) in the exothermic mitochondrial ORR is required for generating sufficient mitochondrial heat that can activate HSF1.

We also anticipate that our ORR-driven thermogenesis model can establish a new connection between mitochondrial respiration and mitochondrial thermogenesis, potentially in all actively respiring cells.
